text:
mai: Heads-up — CS reported multiple customers getting intermittent 503s and 500s from hosted inference around 09:12 UTC. They say some requests also failed with auth/billing errors immediately after the 503s. Can we triage?

jordan: Which customers and a sample request-id?

mai: Customer: NuvoAnalytics (prod). Sample request-id: r-0a9f3c2b. CS attached gateway logs, forwarding below.

support-bot: [auto] Incident alert: hosted-gateway spike: 503-rate 18% (09:10-09:15 UTC). Routing to #incidents.

jordan: grabbing logs...

ops-bot: worker pool 'inference-us-east-3' reported repeated container exits (exit_code=139) across 3 hosts. Recent stderr: "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" followed by segfault stack.

mai: paste of gateway snippet (redacted):
```
GET /v1/generate r-0a9f3c2b 503 upstream: inference-us-east-3-02
Upstream error: worker aborted: signal 11
Model: open-13b-8k-quant
ctx_len: 4096 batch: 48
```

sanjay: 48 batch at 4k ctx on quant model — that's heavy. We had a recent autoscaler change that bumped max-concurrency per-GPU. Could be memory oversubscribe.

chris-oncall: Any coredumps? Can we get the container logs with full backtrace?

ops-bot: Collected last logs from host i-0d4a:
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:36Z] infer-runner[pid=1122]: kv_prefetch: prefetch_size=1.2G
[2026-03-15T09:11:37Z] infer-runner[pid=1122]: cudaMalloc returned NULL
[2026-03-15T09:11:37Z] infer-runner[pid=1122]: signal 11 (SEGV) at 0x7f8c1a2b
*** coredump written to /var/crash/coredump.1122
```

jordan: That matches the OOM -> segfault cascade. Could be a kernel assertion after failed allocation. We should repro locally with the same model + batch + ctx.

mai: CS claims the failures started right after a deploy at 09:05 that changed default 'max_inflight' from 32 -> 64.

sanjay: roll that back ASAP. I'll push a hotfix to revert max_inflight to 32 for hosted pools and restart the pool.

chris-oncall: Meanwhile, can we do a mitigation for impacted customers? Route NuvoAnalytics to a lower-capacity pool or a CPU-only fallback for critical requests. Also add a temporary rate-limit for batch>16.

jordan: Created routing rule: customer.nuvo -> inference-us-east-1-fallback (smaller model) as a stopgap.

support-bot: Customer-facing note draft?

mai: Drafted short update for CS: "We observed transient upstream worker crashes causing 503s when large batched requests hit quantized models after a recent concurrency change. We are rolling back the change and routing affected traffic to fallback pools. We'll follow up with repro details and a timeline." Send?

sanjay: Rollback applied at 09:22 UTC. Restarting inference-us-east-3 runner pool now (graceful drain).

ops-bot: rollback action recorded: config:max_inflight set to 32 on pool inference-us-east-3 by sanjay at 09:22:11 UTC. Pool restart initiated.

mai: After rollback, 503 rate dropped to 0.8% within 3 min. Customer reports reduced errors.

jordan: Repro attempt in staging with same model + ctx + batch 48 hits OOM quickly. Repro log:
```
> python reproduce.py --model open-13b-8k-quant --batch 48 --ctx 4096
Allocating KV cache: 1.1G
Alloc failed: out of memory
RuntimeException: cudaMalloc failed
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

chris-oncall: Good repro. Action items: 1) revert config (done), 2) add a hard guard in runtime to reject batch>32 for quant models with ctx>2048, 3) add kernel-level check to avoid segfault on alloc failure, 4) customer billing check.

mai: On billing: CS noticed some requests returned 500 (internal) and were retried by client; Nuvo says they were billed for retried requests. We need to confirm whether we double-billed and issue credits if so.

support-bot: Billing escalation created INC-3142 assigned to finance-team. Please attach request-ids.

jordan: Collected list of effected request-ids and timestamps and uploaded to INC-3142.

sanjay: I'll open a runtime PR with a fail-first check that returns a 429 or 413 when batch/ctx exceeds safe limits for quant models. Also adding an explicit OOM handler to convert alloc failures into a managed 503 without segfault.

chris-oncall: Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (config bump + unsafe alloc path), mitigation (rollback + routing), permanent fixes, billing credits, and customer comms. Assigning postmortem to mai.

mai: Will take postmortem. ETA initial draft 24h.

jordan: Follow-up: are we sure this is only quant models? Any occurrences on float32 variants?

ops-bot: Telemetry: 92% of aborts in the window were on quantized models (open-13b-8k-quant, opt-6.7b-4k-quant). Float32 variants saw normal error rates.

mai: Thanks team. Keeping this thread open for postmortem link and customer comms.

chris-oncall: Closing mitigation: pool restarted and routing in place. Will monitor for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
